newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila urges Tokyo to review loan rule.
newsitem.headline: Manila urges Tokyo to review loan rule.

text.p: Philippine Finance Secretary Roberto de Ocampo has urged Japan to ease the 35 percent loan loss provision it imposes on Japanese banks lending to Philippine institutions, according to the text of a letter released to reporters on Tuesday.

"It might be worthwhile to revisit the rules governing provisioning for the particular case of the Philippines," de Ocampo said in a letter to Japanese Finance Minister Kubo Wataru, citing the country's improved economic climate.
This requirement was imposed on Japanese banks which lent to countries with rescheduled previous loans. It will remain within five years after the last debt rescheduling.
In the case of the Philippines, this loan requirement will stay until March 1998.
But the requirement means a "heavy disincentive" for Japanese banks to invest in the Philippines since they would have to set as a buffer fund 35 percent of their loan exposure, de Ocampo said.
He added that the loan rule is not consistent with the investment-grade rating given to the Philippines by the Japan Credit Rating Agency.
